elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Revised 14.2: "Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer"; "Deliverable" is defined in 1.4 to include "other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer," so work product is captured.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: Revised 14.2: "Vendor assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable" — present-tense assignment covering the defined Deliverables (which include work product).

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.3: "Vendor retains Vendor Technology"; 1.8 defines Vendor Technology as Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates, etc.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Retained 13.2 grants a "perpetual ... licence" for Vendor Technology "embedded in a Deliverable"; 14.3 cross-refers to that perpetual licence where Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: 13.2: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence" to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: 13.2: "royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business."

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.1: "Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material..." with "No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services."

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.4: "No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights" — default is no joint ownership, and any opt-in requires a signed instrument fixing exploitation rights.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: 14.3 retains Vendor Technology to Vendor and 1.4 excludes from Deliverables "generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The revised 14.2 deletes the Deliverable licence entirely and vests ownership in Customer; no perpetual licence to Deliverables is granted (13.2 covers only Vendor Technology/software, not the Deliverable itself). Not required at the chosen preferred level.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: No Deliverable licence survives in 14.2 after the redline; irrevocability appears only in 13.2 for embedded Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: No worldwide licence to Deliverables in the rendered text; 13.2's "worldwide" applies to software/Vendor Technology only.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No royalty-free Deliverable licence grant remains; the licence sentence in 14.2 was replaced by ownership language.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: No use/modify licence to Deliverables is stated; the right flows from ownership under revised 14.2 rather than from an express licence.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: No sublicensing right to Deliverables is expressed; the redline relies on ownership instead.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: revised 14.2 supplies both Customer ownership of Deliverables (which include work product per 1.4) and Vendor's present assignment, while retained 14.1, 14.3, 13.2 and 14.4 already deliver Customer Data ownership, Vendor's pre-existing IP retention, the perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free embedded-IP licence, and the no-joint-ownership default.

The fallback licence elements are unmet because the redline removes the Deliverable licence rather than upgrading it; this is immaterial since the stronger preferred level (ownership plus assignment) is fully met.

Minimal: a single sentence in 14.2 was replaced, and no extras (survival tails, expense allocation, procedures, extra damages categories) were added; favourable retained language in 13.2, 14.1, 14.3 and 14.4 is untouched.

Preserves intent: 14.3's cross-reference to the Section 13.2 perpetual licence still resolves, the Vendor Technology identification/third-party-material duty survives, and deleting the revocable term-limited licence leaves no dangling term because 10.1 preserves rights in accepted Deliverables according to their terms and ownership now supersedes the licence.
